stem: If a growing child maintains the exact same weight over a six-month period while increasing in height, what is the expected result for their $\text{BMI}$?

options.text: The $\text{BMI}$ z-score will stay the same regardless of height.

explanation: Because $\text{BMI}$ is calculated as weight divided by height squared ($\text{kg}/\text{m}^2$), increasing the denominator while the numerator stays constant results in a lower value.
rationale: Think about the mathematical formula for $\text{BMI}$ where height is in the denominator.

optionExplanations.A: This would only happen if weight gained exceeded the rate of height growth, which is the opposite of the scenario described.
optionExplanations.B: Because $\text{BMI}$ is calculated as weight divided by height squared ($\text{kg}/\text{m}^2$), increasing the denominator while the numerator stays constant results in a lower value.
optionExplanations.C: This ignores the mathematical relationship where height is a primary component of the $\text{BMI}$ calculation.
optionExplanations.D: A z-score is relative to age and gender, but a drop in absolute $\text{BMI}$ through height growth generally shifts the z-score downward.
